requirements.title: Program-sheet year selection
requirements.summary: Use a program sheet from the matriculation year or later; requirements from different sheets cannot be mixed.

requirements.title: Letter-grade requirement and historical exceptions
requirements.summary: Program-sheet courses require letter grades except Spring 2019–20 and Autumn 2020–21 through Summer 2020–21.

requirements.title: No category double-counting
requirements.summary: A program-sheet course may count under only one category; separate CS degree rules identify Writing in the Major exceptions unrelated to AI depth.

requirements.title: Program-sheet approval
requirements.summary: Submit planned/completed courses with units for approval at least one quarter before expected graduation. Only approved sheets proceed to Engineering graduation review; special registration status also requires an approved sheet.

requirements.title: Track completion and changes
requirements.summary: The AI track belongs to the CS BS. Track changes are allowed, but one full CS track must be satisfied before applying to graduate; notify CS through its track-change form after the Axess request.

requirements.title: Exceptions and deviations
requirements.summary: Departures from the published program sheet require a petition for exceptions or deviations; approval is not assumed.

requirements.title: Combined CS program GPA
requirements.summary: The parent CS program requires at least 2.0 GPA across Engineering Fundamentals, CS Core, Depth and Senior Project combined; this is not a separately stated AI-track GPA.

requirements.title: AI depth: course and unit minima
requirements.summary: Both minima apply to distinct depth courses; satisfy A, B, C and the elective requirement.

requirements.title: Track B: select two different areas
requirements.summary: One course from each of two different areas.

requirements.title: Track C: one additional course
requirements.summary: Choose one additional B or C course, or an advisor-approved CS 329 suffix course. Do not reuse a course counted elsewhere.

requirements.title: Advisor-approved CS 329 option
requirements.summary: CS 329 with any suffix requires advisor approval.

requirements.title: At least three additional track electives
requirements.summary: Use B, C, general CS or named additional electives. Up to one eligible humanities course may replace one elective. Extra electives may be needed to reach 25 depth units.

requirements.title: General CS elective pool
requirements.summary: This is an optional pool, not a separately required set. CS 157 or PHIL 151 is one alternative; do not count both as two options.

requirements.title: General elective suffix families
requirements.summary: Any suffix of CS 247, CS 248 or CS 348 is allowed by the program sheet; these are course families rather than invented individual course records.

requirements.title: Prior-year elective eligibility
requirements.summary: A prior-year General CS elective is eligible only if the student was matriculated in that year.

requirements.title: Special elective unit constraints
requirements.summary: CS 195 contributes at most four units; CS 293 must be taken for at least three units.

requirements.title: Humanities substitution limit
requirements.summary: At most one track elective may come from the Bulletin's eligible humanities pool.

requirements.title: Parent CS core and senior project boundary
requirements.summary: The AI sheet places 25 depth units within 43 combined CS Core/Depth/Senior Project units: core is 15 minimum, senior project at least 3. The host degree has additional requirements outside this concentration inventory.

requirements.title: Departmental transfer approval
requirements.summary: Transfer coursework in CS Core, Depth and Senior Project requires Computer Science office approval.

requirements.title: Current-sheet approval deadline
requirements.summary: The final sheet is due no later than one month before the last quarter of senior year; obtain the departmental representative signature and petition/initial/date changes.

requirements.title: Eligible humanities elective pool
requirements.summary: Optional replacement pool, capped at one track elective; cross-listed versions are acceptable.

requirements.title: Course passing grade
requirements.summary: Program-sheet courses require D− or better and letter grading, except approved exceptions.

requirements.title: General elective sequencing
requirements.summary: Complete CS 111 before CS 112 or CS 140E. CS 111 and CS 212 may both count toward the host BS.

requirements.title: Depth transfer and deviation review
requirements.summary: Depth transfer needs CS approval via the course-equivalency form, identifying the Stanford equivalent, external course, timing, units, syllabus and textbook list. Deviations require committee review; petition at least one quarter before applying to graduate, with no approval guarantee.

notes: Official bachelors overview confirms Artificial Intelligence as a formally declared CS track; the same section calls it an AI concentration. Classify as concentration within CS BS, never as a standalone AI degree.
No public syllabus or course-site verification was performed for this discovery.

The official 2026–27 AI PDF viewer is public (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sVHp_i3gvWEo6qKm0GM8NLMWhgwAJyIb/view). Its exact embedded download URL is robots-disallowed. No alternate download or content bypass was attempted; the PDF contents were not inspected.

The 2026–27 Engineering handbook CS page supplies degree overview and suggested research preparation, not the complete AI track inventory. Suggested research courses were not mislabeled as track requirements.
Quarter calendar is evidenced by the program-sheet page explicitly describing academic quarter exceptions and graduation timing. No conversion of source units into semester credits is made.

The Engineering directory independently publishes the 2026–27 spreadsheet. Its permitted HTTP 200 body supplied 135 distinct fixed code options; this did not access or bypass the blocked PDF endpoint. The rendered Bulletin supplied the separate 86-entry humanities pool and verified AI course titles. Raw Bulletin HTTP contains unresolved numeric course IDs and is not treated as named course evidence.

Complete concentration scope covers seven courses/25 depth units, A/B/C/electives, all fixed current pools, suffix-family options, eligible prior-year electives, humanities substitution cap, grades, approval and transfer. Parent CS core/senior totals are context; parent mathematics, science, general education, WIM and capstone inventories are outside this concentration scope.

B requires two courses from different areas; C and electives are additional courses. Up to one humanities option can replace a track elective. Pools can overlap but a course cannot be counted twice. CS 329 requires advisor approval; CS 247/248/348 allow any suffix. A prior-year general elective is eligible only for a student matriculated in that year.

Some fixed elective course titles are not yet transcribed and remain null; all course credit values, descriptions and general prerequisites remain unknown except explicitly represented elective sequencing. Source units remain units, never converted. No public syllabus/site or launch date was verified.

The sheet and Bulletin differ in parent-degree/WIM wording and total context (the sheet mentions at most 95 major units while Bulletin General displays 93). These are not silently reconciled or claimed as whole-degree completeness. The local AI A/B/C and named additional elective pools agree.
